https://www.grandprix.com/news/fia-clear.text: Max Verstappen, British GP 2026 © Red Bull Ferrari and Red Bull developed the device almost simultaneously earlier this season, with Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur jokingly christening it the 'Macarena'. The concept initially worked without major problems, but scrutiny intensified after Max Verstappen crashed twice in quick succession in Austria and Britain. The FIA then demanded additional technical information from both teams and carried out a formal Failure Mode and Effects Analysis. When the first such design appeared, we wanted to ensure that it was absolutely safe, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told Austrian newspaper Osterreich. The governing body examined the mandated closing time of the wing and the car's behaviour after activation. We held very intensive discussions to ensure that we consider these designs safe, Tombazis continued. Our main goal was to eliminate any risk of, for example, a hydraulic failure. Although the concept was ruled safe, Red Bull nevertheless carried out further work on its version after the crashes. Tombazis stressed that those changes were not forced by the FIA, but were made by Red Bull for its own safety reasons. The team temporarily used a different specification before Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar returned to the standard version in Hungary. McLaren is also expected to introduce its own version after the summer break, meaning the unusual concept may now spread further across the grid. (GMM) Grandprix.com context: One day earlier, Grandprix.com reported that Mercedes did not expect to use the Macarena rear wing in 2026 . https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/265471.text: Court Crime Oxfordshire Image released of thug jailed for 'truly appalling' abuse By Toby Oliver Reporter Share 0 Comments 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. An image has been released of a violent thug jailed for 'sustained and truly appalling' abuse of a former partner. Stewart Hayes attacked the woman more than 25 times during their relationship which lasted from December 2024 to January this year. Oxford Crown Court was told that Hayes, 44, also subjected her to psychological abuse which included controlling who she saw, preventing her from going to medical appointments and stealing £32,000 from her. Hayes also told her she had to 'steal to eat'. Matthew Bolt, prosecuting, told the court, at the sentencing on Friday, September 11, that Hayes pleaded guilty to two counts of using controlling and coercive behaviour, and one count of assault, causing actual bodily harm, on the first day of his trial earlier this year. READ MORE: Oxford Romanian food store investigated for illegal tobacco Stewart Hayes (Image: TVP) Mr Bolt said: "He was very controlling. He would go wherever she went and stopped others talking to her." The court heard that one argument ended with Hayes pouring orange juice into her suitcase and breaking all her make-up. Mr Bolt said the victim suffered blows to the head and punches to the jaw. On one occasion, she contacted her parents to get her out. Mr Bolt added: "She was shaking and crying, such was the impact of the offending. "He slammed a door onto her, punched her in the jaw, grabbed her hair and pulled her down stairs. He repeatedly punched her. "It was calculated to separate a vulnerable woman from her support." Hayes was jailed for 40 months and given a 10-year restraining order. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck1w.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Some wreckage was recovered from the water By Makuochi Okafor ,Â BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Lagos Â and Â Basillioh Rukanga Published 6 October 2026 Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has declared three days of national mourning after a military aircraft crashed in southern Ondo State, killing 25 people. Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo on Monday said 32 people had died but on Tuesday the Air Force clarified that 25 people had been killed - five crew and 20 passengers. Authorities say the plane was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when it came down in a swamp near a naval base on Monday morning. After reaching the site, the aircraft was found to be submerged under water, officials said. A resident told the BBC that clothes and shoes had been found at the site. Smoke could be seen rising from the area. It is the deadliest crash involving a Nigerian military aircraft since 1992. The Nigerian Air Force has released the names of those killed, showing that 19 of those on board were military personnel. Tinubu offered his deepest condolences to those killed and has ordered a full investigation. The president also ordered national flags to be flown at half-mast across the country as a mark of respect for those who died. "This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation," Tinubu said. "Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten," he added. The aviation minister earlier said he had been informed "of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today". Keyamo said "efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive" before subsequent confirmation that it had crashed near a naval base in Igbokoda, Ondo state. He said search and rescue efforts were ongoing. The crashed plane, described as an ATR-42 aircraft, carries between 30 and 50 passengers, according to its manufacturers. Image source, Ondo state Image caption, Officials from Ondo state visited the site of the crash Tinubu has ordered the Air Force to immediately begin a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to help prevent similar incidents in the future. The Nigerian Air Force plays a key role in the country's military operations, including efforts to tackle armed groups and insecurity in several parts of the country. In May 2021, Nigeria's army chief, Lt-Gen Ibrahim Attahiru, was killed in a plane crash alongside 10 other officers in the north-western state of Kaduna amid bad weather. In February of the same year, seven people died after a military plane crashed short of a runway in the capital Abuja. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/19/aust.text: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines was deliberately struck by a car and suffered "critical injuries" on Monday in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as an attack.Haines was hurt outside her office in Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northwest of Melbourne, police said.The 65-year-old "suffered what has been described as critical injuries", Victoria Police Acting Superintendent Ashley Mason said, without identifying the victim in line with police custom in Australia.The 43-year-old male driver was detained by civilians, Mason said, and then arrested by police, who found a knife in his car."This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act," Albanese told national broadcaster ABC.He also told journalists: "All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery."The alleged attacker's motive remained unknown, Albanese said, with Australia's counter-terrorism squad activated.The Australian Federal Police has documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation's politicians in recent years.They established a dedicated team last year to investigate groups and individuals targeting lawmakers.Albanese said on Monday that "the temperature has increased in recent times"."I've expressed that concern to people in the media," he said."If you look at anyone's social media feeds and look at the comments, people will say things that they would never say face to face."'Thoroughly decent'Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action.She was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption."This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care," her family said in a statement."We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.""Our family, and Helen's staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media," the statement said.Albanese said Haines was "incredibly hardworking"."She is fiercely intelligent but, most importantly, she's just a thoroughly decent human being," he said.
